name: Adapter
intent: Make an incompatible interface work with code that expects a different one, without changing either side.
scenario: Checkout expects a gateway with pay(dollars). A third-party LegacyBank library only offers makePayment(cents, currency) and returns a result object.
problem: You have working code that talks to PaymentGateway.pay(dollars), and a library you cannot modify that does the same job with different method names, units and return values. Calling the library directly spreads its quirks through your checkout.
solution: Write a small wrapper that implements the interface your code expects and translates each call to the library's own API. Checkout talks to the adapter as if it were any other gateway.
pain: Checkout has an if/else for each payment provider
Dollars-to-cents conversion is repeated at every call site
Forgetting the conversion charges 100 times too little
Adding another provider means editing Checkout again
benefits: All translation lives in one adapter class
A new vendor is a new adapter, no checkout edits
whenToUse: You want to use an existing class or library whose interface does not match what you need
You are integrating third-party or legacy code and want to isolate it behind your own interface
Several similar services should be usable interchangeably
whenNotToUse: You control both sides: change one interface to match
The translation is trivial and used once: call it inline
The mismatch is about behaviour, not shape; an adapter cannot fix a fundamentally different model
pitfalls: Leaky adapters: concepts that do not map cleanly (errors, units, async) bleed through
Layers of adapters on adapters make the real call hard to trace
Adapters hide cost: a cheap-looking call may trigger a heavy conversion
Easy to confuse with Decorator (same interface in and out) and Facade (simplifies many classes)

roles.label: Client
roles.description: Code that works with the target interface.

roles.label: Adapter
roles.description: Implements the target and translates calls to the adaptee.

roles.label: Adaptee
roles.description: The existing class with the incompatible interface.

quiz.question: Your checkout calls PaymentGateway.pay(dollars). A vendor library you cannot edit exposes makePayment(cents, currency). A teammate wants to call the library directly in the three places that charge cards, multiplying by 100 each time. What is the better design?
options: Patch the vendor library so that it accepts dollars, and re-apply the patch on each upgrade
Add a conversion helper and call it from each of the three places before the vendor call
Write a class implementing PaymentGateway that converts the amount and calls makePayment
Subclass Checkout once per vendor and override its charge step with that vendor's call
quiz.explanation: An adapter keeps units and method names in one class, and checkout depends only on PaymentGateway. A helper still leaves vendor calls spread through checkout, and patching a library you do not own breaks on every upgrade.

quiz.question: Your adapter wraps a vendor SDK. Checkout now has `catch (VendorTimeoutException)` imported from the SDK, so a vendor swap would break it. What should change?
options: Return null from the adapter on any vendor error, and let checkout test for null
Keep the catch in checkout, and make the next vendor's adapter throw the same VendorTimeoutException class
Catch the base Exception type in checkout, so no vendor class needs importing there
Have the adapter catch SDK exceptions and throw the app's own PaymentFailed error
quiz.explanation: Errors are part of the interface, so the adapter should translate them into the app's own type and stop the vendor model leaking. Reusing the vendor's class keeps the dependency, a blanket catch hides real bugs, and null loses the reason.

quiz.question: Three payment adapters implement PaymentGateway. Product wants every gateway call logged with its duration, and the code must not change when a fourth vendor is added. Where should this live?
options: Copy the timing code into each of the three adapters, and into the fourth when it arrives
A LoggingGateway that implements PaymentGateway, wraps any gateway and times each call
Add a timing block in Checkout around each call to the gateway, so adapters stay simple
A new TimedPaymentGateway interface that every adapter has to implement from now on
quiz.explanation: A wrapper with the same interface in and out adds behaviour to any gateway, which is the Decorator idea, and works for future vendors. Putting it in each adapter duplicates it, and Checkout would then do work that does not belong to checkout.
